title: Explicit interchange diagrams and their normalized exchange words
statement: Fix a finite commutative ring A. A supplied diagram of f:X→Y and g:Y→Z consists of schemes W,V,P,T and maps a:X→W proper, e:W→V open, r:V→Y proper, k:V→P open, p:P→T proper, i:Y→T open and q:T→Z proper, with a e r=f, i q=g and k p=r i [def-pur-etale-graph-presentation-maps, lem-pur-etale-proper-open-exchange-cube]. Its source, middle and composite presentations are (a,e,r), (id,i,q) and (a,e k,p q). For a proper/open/proper presentation H=(a,e,p), proper a' and open v with a' v=a, shrink(H,a',v)=(a',v e,p). The elementary shrinking isomorphism is the inverse identity-top proper/open exchange from R_a to R_a' J_v, followed by the open compositor under R_p. The diagram interchange is R_a J_e Γ_(k,r,p,i) R_q, after removal of the middle R_id and with canonical open and proper compositors. Γ is the same family chosen with its support and K-injective normalization from the cube theorem, not an arbitrary endpoint isomorphism. All these definitions are moved unchanged from the original interchange module.

This is a new obligation, not a theorem claimed to be proved by that Lean existence declaration.
